lessons.title: Beginning Sounds

teach.intro: Every word starts with a sound! Say a word slowly and listen to the very first sound you hear.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the /b/ sound?
Which word starts with the /s/ sound?
Which word starts with the /m/ sound?
Which word starts with the /f/ sound?

lessons.review: You just practiced listening for the very first sound in a word. Try it with words around your house!

lessons.title: Ending Sounds

teach.intro: Words also end with a sound! Listen closely to the very last sound you hear.

questions.prompt: Which word ends with the /t/ sound?
Which word ends with the /g/ sound?
Which word ends with the /n/ sound?
Which word ends with the /p/ sound?

lessons.review: Great work noticing ending sounds! This helps with spelling later on.

lessons.title: Rhyming Words

teach.intro: Rhyming words sound the same at the end, even though they start differently.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'cat'?
Which word rhymes with 'log'?
Which word rhymes with 'bee'?
Which word rhymes with 'pan'?

lessons.review: Rhyming helps you hear patterns in words, which makes reading easier!

lessons.title: Sight Words

teach.intro: Some words show up so often we learn to recognize them right away, just by sight!

questions.prompt: Which word says 'the'?
Which word says 'and'?
Which word says 'is'?
Which word says 'you'?

lessons.review: Knowing sight words by heart makes reading sentences much faster!

lessons.title: Story Time: What Happened?

teach.intro: When we read or listen to a story, we think about what happened, who did it, and where.
examples: Sam has a red ball -> the ball is red
The dog ran to the park -> the dog went to the park

questions.prompt: Sam has a red ball. What color is the ball?
The dog ran to the park. Where did the dog go?
Mia ate an apple for lunch. What did Mia eat?

lessons.review: Thinking about the details in a story helps you understand and remember it.

lessons.title: Blending Sounds Into Words

teach.intro: You can blend, or push together, letter sounds to read a whole word.

questions.prompt: What word do these sounds make: c-a-t?
What word do these sounds make: d-o-g?
What word do these sounds make: s-u-n?
What word do these sounds make: m-a-p?

lessons.review: Blending sounds together is one of the most important reading skills!

lessons.title: Sneaky Sound Teams (sh, ch, th)

teach.intro: Sometimes two letters team up to make one new sound, like sh, ch, and th.

questions.prompt: Which word has the /sh/ sound?
Which word has the /ch/ sound?
Which word has the /th/ sound?
Which word has the /sh/ sound?

lessons.review: Sound teams like sh, ch, and th show up in tons of words - great spotting!

lessons.title: Compound Words

teach.intro: Two small words can join together to make one new word.

questions.prompt: Sun + flower = ?
Back + pack = ?
Cup + cake = ?
Rain + bow = ?

lessons.review: Compound words are a fun way to build bigger words from small ones!

lessons.title: What Happened First, Next, Last?

teach.intro: Stories happen in order: a beginning, a middle, and an end.

questions.prompt: Sam woke up, ate breakfast, then went to school. What happened first?
What happened after Sam woke up?
What happened last?

lessons.review: Putting events in order helps you retell stories clearly!

lessons.title: Opposites

teach.intro: Opposites are words that mean completely different things, like hot and cold.
examples: Hot is the opposite of Cold
Big is the opposite of Small
Up is the opposite of Down

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of hot?
What is the opposite of big?
What is the opposite of up?
What is the opposite of happy?

lessons.review: Learning opposites helps you describe the world more clearly!
